narratives.Overview:
Split from #4383 later-arc.

## Pain

After #4383 parks setup-created scopes in `pending/` and the operator mints `scope:record-approved-scope`, a later worker still hits `verify:intent-constraint` mint-mid-build. That gate selects running xBRIEFs, fails with no merge-base mint, and its remedy verb is `scope:record-intent-constraint` behind the same human-presence gate. The approved-scope digest does not satisfy it. The operator has left.

## What this is not

- Not #4383 (`record-approved-scope` ask at Phase 0f, `promote --batch` dwell, decline reader on Step 0.5 Scan).
- Not emptying `file_scope` as a back-out.

## Origin

#4383 pain-audit 5688229241 F1: relief bound to one mint verb; two sibling gates reproduce mint-mid-build after Phase B. Recut 5688246245 named this as uncovered residual.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-15T23:47:31Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Open critique of #4587 at dispatch-sha `f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352`. Ceiling 5689608688 honored (Stop 1 write-back; no later thread comments read). Pin reads are `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:<path>`. Dest vitest did not start (`vitest` unresolved from `vitest.config.ts`); re-verification is those pin-reads plus the evaluate/mint tests at that SHA, not a live run.

The pain is real. The leftover cannot bind as a recut of `verify:intent-constraint`, and it cannot bind as a sibling mint at the `record-approved-scope` ask. Existing machinery already snapshots facts, mints on merge-base, and refuses same-PR rewrite. What is missing is an operator-present invoker at the moment `value` / `unit` / `rejectionScope` exist.

## 1. P1 cannot bind as a gate recut — blocks-the-design

Evidence. `packages/core/src/intent-constraint/evaluate.ts` already fail-closes the story the issue names, and only that story:

- No changed production `.ts`/`.js` → skip (`evaluate.ts` N/A branch; test `skips when no production .ts/.js changed`).
- Changed production, no new throw/reject/abort/numeric-const → pass (`evaluate.ts` `no new throw/reject/abort sites or numeric consts`; tests `passes quiet with no new facts` and `leaves skip/filter/return-error without new const or throw as leftover pass`).
- New facts, unique running xBRIEF, no mint for that `planId` → exit 1 `no merge-base mint record for planId` (`evaluate.ts` after `resolveCurrentPlanId`; test `fails when --plan-id does not match merge-base mint`).
- Same-PR rewrite of `.deft/intent-constraint/` → exit 1 (`evaluate.ts` `same-PR rewrite`; test `fails same-PR mint rewrite`).
- Authority is `git show <merge-base>` only (`content/docs/intent-constraint.md` contract item 6). Tests and in-scope paths are not authority (test `does not treat tests or in-scope paths as authority`).
- `listBaseRecords` reads only `.deft/intent-constraint/`. `.deft/approved-scope/` is a different directory and schema. No evaluate path consults an approved-scope digest.

`extract.ts` treats one `throw` statement in changed production source as a `throw-site`. The origin concrete case (worker adds one `throw`) is the posted fixture in `evaluate.test.ts`.

Failure mode. The issue is labeled `bug` and states mint-mid-build as the defect, with no fence that the snapshot stays. A builder who "stops the later worker hitting the gate" by skipping when the mint is absent, by allowing same-PR rewrite, or by letting an approved-scope digest authorize throw sites, inverts first-ship #4541. Gate-integrity forbids clearing that red by editing the gate.

Disposition consequence. This leftover binds only as operator-ask / discovery placement for the mint #4541 already specified. It does not bind as a change to `evaluateIntentConstraint`, as approved-scope covering constraints, or as a second snapshot.

## 2. The approved-scope operator moment cannot mint this record — blocks-the-design

Evidence. `scope:record-intent-constraint` copies `plan["x-directive/intentConstraint"]` (`packages/cli/src/scope-record-intent-constraint.ts`). `parseIntentConstraintContract` returns `missing plan["x-directive/intentConstraint"]` when that key is absent (`mint.ts`). The pending-path CLI test mints only because its fixture already contains `constraints: [{ value: "1024", unit: "bytes", rejectionScope: "invocation" }]`.

`git grep x-directive/intentConstraint` at this SHA hits mint/types/tests only. Zero hits under `content/skills/` or `content/templates/`. Setup `SKILL.md` collects operator-named `file_scope` and forbids minting an approved-scope digest; it does not author the intent-constraint plan key.

`uncoveredDeltas` (`diff.ts`) is one mint row → at most one numeric-const of that value and at most one throw/reject/abort, and the numeric and rejection slots must share a path. A placeholder mint at allocation does not cover later facts.

Dest Phase 0f still confirms promote **and** activate through Step 0.5 (`content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-0.md`). The park-in-pending world is the #4383 recut, not this tree. That does not make P1 future-only: the mint key is equally absent today.

Failure mode. A Bound remedy that prints `scope:record-intent-constraint` next to `scope:record-approved-scope` has the operator run a verb that exits 2 on every setup-created brief. A Bound remedy that fills speculative `value`/`unit`/`rejectionScope` so the verb succeeds attests numbers that later `uncoveredDeltas` will not match, and same-PR rewrite still forbids fixing the mint in the implementation PR. Either way the later worker still fails, which is the pain this leftover exists to close.

Disposition consequence. P1 is not "the third verb at the approved-scope ask." Any ask belongs at plan-key authorship, before the implementation PR that introduces the facts — the sequence item 6 already writes. File-scope can be named at allocation. Throw values usually cannot.

## 3. "A later worker still hits" omits the new-facts conjunct — sharpens-framing

Evidence. Same pass branches as finding 1. A numeric literal only in an `if` condition is leftover, not a fact (docs item 3; leftover-pass test). `listRunningPlanIds` reads `xbrief/active/` with `plan.status === "running"` only. The `no merge-base mint record for planId` string is the post-activate unique-running path, not the zero-record path (`unapproved constraint or rejection scope in ${listed}`).

Failure mode. A total allocation-time mint for every setup-created scope would demand constraints for stories that never add a throw or numeric-const, and would mis-teach the fail string for the zero-record case.

Disposition consequence. P1 is: changed production `.ts`/`.js` with a new throw/reject/abort or numeric-const, running xBRIEF, no merge-base mint for that `planId`, operator already gone. Not "any later worker."

## 4. The fail path and the skills do not name the mint verb — sharpens-framing

Evidence. Gate message appends `INTENT_CONSTRAINT_MISSING: Link the hard constraint…` (`types.ts`). `named-cause.ts` remedy for `verify:intent-constraint` is the same sentence, still without `scope:record-intent-constraint`. `git grep record-intent-constraint` over `content/skills/` and `content/templates/` is empty. The verb exists in `tasks/scope.yml`, the CLI, and `content/docs/intent-constraint.md` item 6.

Failure mode. The worker who hits P1 is told to link a constraint to a base-approved requirement, not which verb to run, in which shell, with which human-presence factors. That is the same discoverability hole #4383 measured for `record-approved-scope`, on this sibling.

Disposition consequence. Placement work includes the string the worker sees at `task check`, not only an ask at setup.

## 5. Census — footnote

No disposition weight. Origin comments 5688229241 F1 and 5688246245 match dest: sibling gates, human-presence module shared, approved-scope digest disjoint. `human-presence-mint.ts` is imported by the intent-constraint CLI; agent/CI markers refuse. Sibling leftovers were not treated as targets. Audit-targets none.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered: authority (who may mint), untrusted xBRIEF plan key, shared `.deft/intent-constraint/`, C1/headless cannot mint.

The mint copies agent-writable `plan["x-directive/intentConstraint"]` then asks a human to type `mint`. The human-presence gate proves presence, not that the human named `value`/`unit`/`rejectionScope`. An ask that has the agent fill those fields and the operator attest them stamps agent-chosen limits. That seam is already in #4541; a leftover that adds an invoker must not widen it by inventing paths or values.

C1: a headless worker that adds a `throw` fails `task check` with no operator on the TTY. Fail-closed is correct; the leftover should state that consequence rather than imply a paste-ready mint inside the agent shell.

If a later map prints a copy-paste argv, construct it from a path that already passed the mint's in-root check and quote it. Do not interpolate an agent-written slug into the one shell agents are excluded from.

## Road not taken

I considered scoring this as no leftover: docs item 6 already says mint on the merge base before the implementation PR, so mint-mid-build is the gate working. I did not lean it. Setup and the build/swarm skills never author the plan key and never name the verb, so that sequence has no operator-present invoker on the setup path. That is a placement hole. It is not a missing snapshot.

I also considered treating Phase 0f as the obvious ask, on the grounds that the origin pain-audit asked for the mint family. Dest mint CLI plus missing plan key falsify that clone (finding 2).

## Steelman

The write-up is a clean leftover: one gate, one verb, approved-scope does not cover it, operator has left. `evaluate.ts` after a unique running activate is the measured fail. That is enough to file.

It does not survive as a next-build contract. It does not fence the snapshot. It does not name the plan-key precondition. It states "a later worker still hits" without the new-facts conjunct. Built as written, the two available readings are a gate recut and a sibling-verb print that exits 2.

What would flip the blocking findings, both restatements rather than new machinery: (1) the snapshot, merge-base authority, and same-PR rewrite stay; (2) P1 includes the new-facts conjunct; (3) any operator ask is at plan-key authorship, not at `record-approved-scope`; (4) the fail string or the skill that hits the gate names `scope:record-intent-constraint`.

## Verdict

P1 is a real setup-path placement hole on a live, required check-aggregate gate (`gate-lists.ts` framework and consumer lists; `tasks/verify.yml`). The approved-scope digest does not satisfy it. The leftover cannot bind as a recut of #4541 and cannot bind as the third verb at the approved-scope ask. Existing mint + evaluate already implement the snapshot. Specify the invoker for that mint when the constraint values exist, and make the fail path name the verb.
